newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: AIR PORTUGAL PILOTS' STRIKE ENTERS SECOND DAY.
newsitem.headline: AIR PORTUGAL PILOTS' STRIKE ENTERS SECOND DAY.

text.p: State carrier TAP-Air Portugal cancelled three flights on Sunday morning and expected to call off three more later in the second day of an indefinite, selective strike by pilots over working hours, officials said.

The local news agency Lusa quoted a TAP official as saying three flights to Madeira, Barcelona and Dublin had been cancelled and that three evening flights, to London, Madrid and Ponta Delgada in the Azores, were expected to be called off.
The pilots were operating planned flights as normal but were staying away from non-scheduled flights, officials said.
A TAP official told Reuters on Saturday that five flights had been cancelled that day as pilots began their stoppage a few hours ahead of its expected start at midnight (2300 GMT Saturday).
The pilots are protesting over what they say is TAP's inefficient organisation of their working hours.
Officials said the strike could affect at least 15 percent of TAP's flights and could cost the airline at least three billion escudos ($16.2 million) in August.
Government officials have warned that the walkout could cause severe financial problems for the loss-making airline leading to its eventual closure.
Senior government officials were due to meet representatives of the pilots' union on Sunday to try to resolve the dispute, TSF radio reported.
TAP and pilot union officials were not available for comment.
In April, a two-day TAP pilots' stoppage over working hours halted international flights and delayed about 14,000 passengers.
